plain_definition: A US federal law that lets Congress vote to overturn a recently issued federal agency regulation. If both the House and Senate pass a joint resolution of disapproval and the President signs it (or Congress overrides a veto), the disapproved regulation has no force or effect -- treated in law as if the agency had never issued it -- and the agency generally cannot reissue a substantially similar rule without new legislative authority.
formal_definition: 5 U.S.C. 801-802. Section 801(a)(1) requires an agency to submit each new rule to Congress before it can take effect; Section 802 sets out the expedited procedure for a joint resolution of disapproval. A joint resolution disapproving a specific rule, once enacted, states that the disapproved rule 'shall have no force or effect' -- the operative language of, for example, Public Law 119-5 (10 April 2025), which disapproved an IRS digital-asset broker reporting rule.
